description:
We're a team of people who care about climate data and want to put it to work. Wildfires are spreading faster and harder every year. We believe that data can help us see the patterns hiding in the noise: propagation (wind, fire, etc.) , fuel, terrain, timing. 

Our vision is to create a better world for the future of tomorrow. If you share the same ideals - join us in Vienna
summary: Moonpies harmonizes NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS hot spot data with Meteomatics weather data to analyze fire risk across Europe. The project provides an interactive web interface for exploring correlations between fire events and weather conditions through maps and time series visualizations.
details:
Moonpies harmonizes NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS hot spot data with Meteomatics weather data to analyze wildfire risk across Europe. The system follows a pipeline architecture of data ingestion, processing, and visualization. It fetches fire and weather datasets independently, then merges them using spatial and temporal alignment. The processed data powers a Flask web application with interactive maps and time series charts.

The project transforms raw satellite and meteorological data into actionable insights, enabling identification of weather patterns that precede fire events. It supports early warning systems and risk assessment through an intuitive interface. By revealing correlations between weather conditions and fire activity, Moonpies aims to improve wildfire prediction and prevention strategies across Europe.

The project uses Python 3.11+, Flask, uv package manager, NASA FIRMS API, and Meteomatics weather API. It creatively bridges satellite fire detection with meteorological observations using spatial-temporal alignment. Key considerations included handling data heterogeneity between different sources, efficient processing of large Europe-scale datasets, and building an intuitive interface for non-technical users. The modular design allows for extensibility to other regions and data sources.
